title: The Moon’s Changing Shape
description: Recognize the words used for the Moon’s illuminated shapes as seen from Earth during its monthly cycle.
cardDescription: Recognize the words used for the Moon’s illuminated shapes as seen from Earth during its monthly cycle.
focus: Moon phases describe how much of the sunlit half we see. They normally result from the changing viewing geometry, rather than Earth casting a shadow on the Moon.
solvingTip: A clue about increasing or decreasing illumination asks for a change word. A shape clue asks for a named phase.
words: One of the Moon's apparent illuminated shapes
Moon shape showing less than half its face as a curved sliver
Phase name used when half the Moon's visible disk is lit
Growing in visible illuminated area, as the Moon does
Decreasing in visible illuminated area after a full Moon
Earth's natural satellite whose phases we observe
Phase in which the Moon's visible disk appears entirely lit
Moon phase usually hidden from our view
Moon shape illuminated more than half but less than completely
Path followed by the Moon around Earth
Sunshine reflected from the lunar surface
Planet from which these lunar shapes are viewed
Star supplying the illumination reflected by the Moon
Periodic rise and fall of sea level influenced strongly by the Moon

answerNotes.PHASE: Phases depend on the positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon. Earth's shadow produces a lunar eclipse rather than the usual monthly phase sequence.
answerNotes.CRESCENT: A crescent shows less than half of the apparent lunar disk illuminated. Gibbous describes more than half but less than full.
answerNotes.QUARTER: Quarter refers to the Moon's progress around its cycle. The visible illuminated portion at this phase looks like half a disk.
answerNotes.WAXING: Waxing describes increasing illumination as seen from Earth. Waning describes the decrease.
answerNotes.WANING: Waning concerns the apparent lit portion. The Moon itself is not shrinking.

title: Stars and Familiar Sky Patterns
description: Find recognizable northern sky names alongside the ordinary words used to describe lights and patterns overhead.
cardDescription: Find recognizable northern sky names alongside the ordinary words used to describe lights and patterns overhead.
focus: Some familiar sky patterns are parts of larger constellations. The clues distinguish the Big Dipper from its constellation and identify Polaris by its position rather than its brightness.
solvingTip: Proper names are supported by direct descriptions. The short direction and shape words can provide useful crossing letters.
words: Constellation named for a hunter and known for three belt stars
Big ___, familiar seven-star pattern within Ursa Major
Star near the north celestial pole, also called the North Star
Animal represented by the constellation name Ursa Major
Recognizable arrangement of points in the night sky
Distant luminous body seen as a point at night
Direction associated with the pole near Polaris
Apparent dome overhead where constellations are seen
Three-star feature in the middle of Orion
Figure represented by the constellation Orion
Tiny dotlike appearance of a distant light
Visible energy reaching us from a star
Dark part of the day suited to seeing many stars
Group of stars physically associated in space

answerNotes.ORION: Orion is a constellation. Its three prominent belt stars form one easily recognized pattern within it.
answerNotes.DIPPER: The Big Dipper is an asterism within Ursa Major. It is not a separate constellation.
answerNotes.POLARIS: Polaris is useful as a northern direction marker. It is not the brightest star in the night sky.
answerNotes.BEAR: Ursa Major means Great Bear. The Big Dipper occupies part of that larger constellation.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star, even though it looks very different from the distant points we see at night.

title: A Telescope on Its Tripod
description: Look at the parts of a small telescope and the support that keeps its view steady.
cardDescription: Look at the parts of a small telescope and the support that keeps its view steady.
focus: Different telescope designs gather light with lenses, mirrors, or both. The clues identify parts by their roles, separating the main opening, viewing component, and supporting structure.
solvingTip: Identify the job first: gathering light, sharpening the image, looking through it, or holding the instrument still.
words: Instrument that gathers light to show distant objects in detail
Small viewing component at the observer's end of a telescope
Diameter of a telescope's main light-gathering opening
Three-legged stand supporting a small telescope
Adjustment that makes the viewed image appear sharp
Curved transparent optical piece used in a refracting design
Reflecting optical surface used in a reflecting design
Long body holding a small telescope's optical parts
Support that holds and aims the optical tube
Transparent material used in many optical lenses
Removable cover protecting the front opening
Optical representation formed by collected light
Small turning control used for an adjustment

answerNotes.TELESCOPE: A telescope gathers light to form an image. Its design determines whether lenses, mirrors, or a combination do the main optical work.
answerNotes.EYEPIECE: The eyepiece is where the observer looks. It is distinct from the main lens or mirror gathering light.
answerNotes.APERTURE: Aperture describes the size of the opening. It is not another word for magnification.
answerNotes.TRIPOD: Three legs provide a stable support on a range of surfaces. The mount above them holds and aims the instrument.
answerNotes.FOCUS: Focus changes image sharpness. Merely making an image larger does not guarantee that it will look clearer.

title: Neighbors in the Solar System
description: Name the eight planets and the familiar objects and motions associated with the Sun’s planetary system.
cardDescription: Name the eight planets and the familiar objects and motions associated with the Sun’s planetary system.
focus: This scene uses the modern eight-planet grouping. Planet names are paired with clear distinguishing descriptions, while the shorter clues concern paths, satellites, and the central star.
solvingTip: Read each planet’s defining feature carefully. Order, size, and a familiar visible characteristic provide different routes to an answer.
words: Planet with the smallest orbit around the Sun
Second planet from the Sun, often called the Evening Star
Largest planet in our solar system
Seventh planet from the Sun, with a strongly tilted axis
Category shared by the eight major worlds orbiting our Sun
Third planet from the Sun and our home
Fourth planet, often nicknamed the Red Planet
Sixth planet, especially known for its prominent ring system
Eighth and most distant of the eight planets
Path of a planet around its star
Star at the center of our planetary system
Band of orbiting material especially prominent around Saturn

answerNotes.MERCURY: Mercury is the innermost of the eight planets. Its name here refers to a planet rather than a metallic element.
answerNotes.VENUS: Venus is a planet despite its familiar star nickname. It can also appear as the Morning Star.
answerNotes.JUPITER: Jupiter is a giant planet. Being the largest does not make it the closest to the Sun.
answerNotes.URANUS: Uranus rotates with its axis tilted greatly relative to its orbital plane. The clue also gives its position in planetary order.
answerNotes.PLANET: The modern list contains eight planets. Pluto is classified as a dwarf planet rather than a ninth member of that list.

title: Meteors and Comets
description: Separate the names for icy visitors, rocky space bodies, and the brief streaks seen when material enters our atmosphere.
cardDescription: Separate the names for icy visitors, rocky space bodies, and the brief streaks seen when material enters our atmosphere.
focus: A space object, an atmospheric light event, and a surviving piece on the ground have different names. Comet tails also have a direction set mainly by the Sun’s influence.
solvingTip: Pay attention to location: in space, glowing in the atmosphere, or on the ground. Each location suggests a different term.
words: Luminous streak produced when a small space body enters the atmosphere
Piece of space material that survives its fall to the ground
Icy solar-system body that may develop a glowing head and tails
Small rocky body orbiting the Sun, many found between Mars and Jupiter
Streaming material extending away from a comet's head
Fine particles released by an active comet
Frozen material present in a comet's nucleus
Solid mineral material common in an asteroid
Curving route followed by a comet around the Sun
Brief bright line a meteor makes across the sky
Overhead region where a meteor shower is observed
Star whose heat can activate a comet
Soft or steady light surrounding an active comet's head
Region where an asteroid travels before approaching Earth

answerNotes.METEOR: A meteor is the light phenomenon. The incoming body is a meteoroid, and a surviving piece reaching the ground is a meteorite.
answerNotes.METEORITE: A meteorite is material recovered on the ground. It differs from the brief visible meteor seen during atmospheric entry.
answerNotes.COMET: A comet can release gas and dust as it approaches the Sun. Its tails do not simply trail behind its direction of travel.
answerNotes.ASTEROID: Asteroids are generally rocky bodies. The belt between Mars and Jupiter contains many, though not all, of them.
answerNotes.TAIL: The Sun's radiation and solar wind shape comet tails. A tail generally points away from the Sun rather than directly backward along the orbit.
